sentences.text: Service is complete and Mr. Himmat Singh, learned counsel appears for the respondent.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
Learned counsel for the petitioner-wife submitted that the marriage between the petitioner-wife and respondent-husband was solemnized according to Hindu rites on 02.12.2014.
Out of this wedlock, a male child named Yuvraj was born on 07.07.2017.

The petitioner-wife has been subjected to cruelty, harassment, and maltreatment, which ultimately led to the breakdown of the marriage.
Numerous cases have been filed against each other by the parties.

During the course of litigation, the petitioner filed a criminal complaint, which was registered, and F.I.R. No. 517/2023 was lodged at P.S. sentences.text: This case is pending before the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Beawar, in Original Case No.218/2023.
Additionally, the petitioner has filed Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 1002/2023 before the Family Court No. 1, Jodhpur, under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act.

She has also filed Civil Original Case No. 30/2023 under Section 7 read with Section 25 of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, as well as under Sections 6 and 13 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956.

Furthermore,
she has initiated proceedings under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, and filed Criminal Case No. 125 Cr.P.C. in Jodhpur.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Counsel for the petitioner also mentioned that the respondent has filed a case under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, at Beawar, which was transferred to Jodhpur by the co-ordinate bench of this court in S.B. Civil Transfer Application No. 94/2024 on 24.04.2025.
Learned counsel further submitted that the petitioner is a lady residing at her parental residence in Jodhpur with her widow mother.
Her minor son is studying in Jodhpur, and there is no [2025:RJ-JD:29993] (3 of 4) [CRLTP-11/2025] other family member to look after him.
Traveling alone over a distance of 160 kilometers from Jodhpur to Beawar, Ajmer, for the proceedings would be extremely difficult for her.
She is also a professional dentist, managing a dental clinic in Jodhpur to earn her livelihood for herself and her son.

In light of the aforementioned facts and circumstances, and considering that the cases instituted by the petitioner-wife are pending in Jodhpur, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that, in the interest of justice, the case filed by the respondent- husband currently pending before the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Beawar, Ajmer, should be transferred to the Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Jodhpur.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Beawar, Ajmer
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent vehemently opposed the transfer petition.
It is settled law while considering transfer of case in matrimonial proceedings instituted by the husband, the convenience of the wife is to be looked into.

In this regard, recently, Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the matter of N.C.V. Aishwarya Vs. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, (Civil Appeal No.
4894/2022 arising out of SLP (C) no. 16465/2021) decided on 18.07.2022, while considering transfer of matrimonial case under Section 24 CPC, has observed as under:-
"The cardinal principle for exercise of power under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.

entities.text: N.C.V. Aishwarya Vs. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In matrimonial maters, wherever Courts are called upon to consider the plea of transfer, the Court have to take [2025:RJ-JD:29993] (4 of 4)
[CRLTP-11/2025] into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behaviour pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood and under whose protective umbrella they are seeking their Deepika Sankhla vs Amit Singh Chouhan (2025:Rj-Jd:29993) on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160823445/
2 sustenance to life.

entities.text: Deepika Sankhla vs Amit Singh Chouhan (2025:Rj-Jd:29993)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Given the prevailing socio-economic paradigm in the Indian Society, generally, it is the wife's convenience which must be looked at while considering transfer."

Having considered the submissions made on behalf of the parties, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case noticed above and the settled position of law by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of N.C.V. Aishwarya (supra), the transfer application is allowed.

It is ordered that the Criminal Original Case No.218/2023 pending in the Addl. Cheif Judical Magistrate Beawar,
District Ajmer filed under section 498A and 406 I.P.C. be transferred to the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jodhpur.

entities.label: COURT

A copy of this order be sent to the Addl. Cheif Judical Magistrate Beawar, District Ajmer and Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Jodhpur forthwith.
Stay application also stands disposed of.
